title: how every coldstart process gets V8's linear regex fallback
summary: Every process coldstart runs (CLI, MCP server and keeper via src/index.ts, plus the 12 hook scripts init wires) turns on V8's --enable-experimental-regexp-engine-on-excessive-backtracks by importing hooks/regex-engine.mjs as its FIRST import, so a backtracking regex that blows up is re-run on V8's linear engine and finishes in milliseconds. The ordering is the whole mechanism: the flag only covers regexes created after it is set (a module-level literal created before it still hung), and ES modules run in import order, so a first import covers every module loaded after it. Regexes the linear engine rejects (backreferences, lookarounds) keep backtracking and fall to the 5s parse time limit.

steps.role: sets the V8 flag via node:v8 setFlagsFromString, wrapped in try/catch
imports it first; the keeper is spawned from the same entry (process.argv[1]), so CLI, MCP and keeper are covered
pins the effect in a fresh process and the first-import rule for index.ts + every hook init wires

invariants: hooks/regex-engine.mjs must be the first import of src/index.ts and of every wired hook script; a new hook entry needs it too (the test derives the list from init's HOOK constants).
Measured: parse output byte-identical with the flag on vs off (monica, ripgrep, serilog, coldstart), same speed.
